indicators.label: Buddhist (%)
indicators.description: Share of the district's enumerated religion population reporting Buddhist, the declared reference group. This is the reference-group share of the six-category DCS frame, not a measure of affiliation versus non-affiliation; the DCS frame carries no no-religion category, so a full-affiliation share would be a flat 100 everywhere and carry no signal. Minority-share two-slot design (docs/development/minority-share-metric.md, ratified 2026-07-11). The reference group is Buddhist, Sri Lanka's largest published religion category nationally in the most recent wave (2024). It is declared once and held constant across every wave and area. National Buddhist share as evidence (share of the DCS published national religion population; 2001 uses the 18-district published total): 1981 69.2968%, 2001 76.7087%, 2012 70.1004%, 2024 69.7789% (2024 is the most-recent-wave national share fixing the reference group).
indicators.method: 100 times the district Buddhist count divided by the district total religion population; null where religion was not enumerated (the seven 2001 northern and eastern districts) or the district did not exist (Kilinochchi 1981). religious_change (runtime-derived) differences this reference-group share across consecutive waves; the eight null-coverage rows break the chain where the data dictate.

indicators.method: 100 times the sum of the five non-reference religion categories divided by the district total, equivalently 100 minus the Buddhist share; the two slots are exact complements in every enumerated row. Null on the same eight non-enumerated rows as the reference-group share.
